output.name: Skarún

output.myth: When Aun cut the string, the sky drifted off so far that nobody could fly back to the islands to mend the nets. Ennu sat up all winter with sailcloth and cod-bone and made a hawk to frighten the gulls off the drying racks. It had wings wide enough to shade a boat, and a belly full of stones so it would hold its place. The gulls went shrieking to Tavo, who laughed and lifted the hawk by one wingtip. It went up past the Spindle and hung over the Reach, wings out, and it has never come down. My grandmother's mother said you can see it on still nights, low in the north, when the gulls are quiet. Ennu told it to wait until the gulls learned manners. The gulls have not learned manners. So the hawk keeps its wings out over nets that are gone. Mend your own net, child, and keep one eye up.
output.verse:
Wings spread on the net,
the gulls keep their thieving hours,
the hawk waits above.
